rubric_basis: V10 fixed protocol sections 1, 4, 6-8; source semantics, qualifications, attribution, source/version and boundary fidelity; not a new performance threshold

reviews.source_review_note: Paragraph 49 supports joint participation, Bama and 28-31 January. The 27 January start in the companion remains a source disagreement, not a second visit.
Paragraph 54 supports joint Forum participation. LCBC, not the two representatives, launched the policy and study. Do not replace participation with sole organization.
Paragraph 53 explicitly preserves more than 30 participants, 26-27 February and workplan adoption. Adoption is not verified implementation.
Section B and paragraph 50 place the 30 January side event within the CNMC function. CNMC chair capacity remains separate; this is not evidence of an internal clearance procedure.
Paragraph 57 records 17 December in the report period that includes December 2024. The Yaounde review workshop remains pre-2025 context, with validation prospective.
Paragraphs 66-69 contain Secretary-General observations and recommendations. Preserve the UNOWAS reporting context; no claim of verified internal approval mechanics.
The 3 April briefer describes January travel with the UNOCA head and Bama. Do not import an exact start day or all source-page population estimates into this selected claim.
The briefer connects Forum participation with new financing and reconciliation mechanisms. Participation is not sole organization or an independently counted new Forum.
Page 4 calls the joint February event a conference. Retain that source wording alongside the report workshop identity; do not create another event.
Page 2 attributes a recent withdrawal announcement to Niger. The statement date is known; physical withdrawal and a later implementation status are not established here.
Pages 3-4 contain the briefer's political assessments and priorities. They remain attributable to that speaker and office, not generic shared factual assertions.
Paragraph 61 begins on the preceding page and gives 27-31 January. The retained page locator includes the date passage; no silent correction of UNOWAS's 28 January.
Paragraph 62 specifies representative attendance on 29 January and cites S/2025/187. This does not delimit the entire Forum's duration.
Paragraph 65 identifies the two co-organizers, Dakar, 26-27 February and the UNOWAS report reference. The referral does not prove funded editorial duplication.
The second sentence of paragraph 65 identifies a collection published during the event under UNOCA leadership. It is a publication, not another workshop or proof of exact online release time.
Paragraph 67 records an online 8 April exchange and agreed joint initiatives. This is an observed coordination baseline, not a newly avoided meeting.
Paragraph 63 explicitly cites UNOWAS for the 17 December maritime workshop. Preserve 2024 context and the distinction between technical review and later validation.
Paragraphs 68-70 contain the Secretary-General's Central Africa assessments. Retaining an analytical boundary does not verify internal authorship or clearance steps.
Page 3 explicitly identifies the 3 April UNOWAS statement and S/PV.9890. Keep attributed announcement and the two statement dates, not completed withdrawal.
Pages 3-4 contain the UNOCA briefer's country and regional judgments. The support sheet must not convert them into agreed cross-office positions.
Paragraph 4 records six initiatives announced in Geneva and points to S/2025/448. Announcement is not delivery of all six initiatives.
Paragraph 4 gives 17-18 March and lists the agreed initiatives. The six-item interpretation is corroborated within the same report; it is not six completed projects.
Paragraph 30 explicitly says the 5 May inaugural meeting was co-facilitated by good offices and UNFICYP. No attendance figure is provided.
Paragraph 5 describes leaders jointly launching the Youth Technical Committee on 5 May. Preserve leaders' launch and UN co-facilitation as distinct roles.
Paragraphs 15-16 support 13 committees, over 130 meetings, just over 200 members and 52/48 percentages. Membership and meetings are separate denominators.
Paragraph 35 says the existing crossing enlargement was planned to commence in September. No actual commencement is inferred from this July report.
Paragraph 18 expects the existing crossing expansion to start in September 2025. Preserve expected rather than commenced.
Paragraph 27 is the Secretary-General's encouragement to reach an agreement. Treat the claim as an attributed recommendation, not an agreement or a jointly endorsed position.
Paragraph 31 prints EUR15.2 million and EUR4.12 billion with its export definition. The comparator conflict remains unresolved and blocks a harmonized ratio.
Paragraph 24 prints EUR15.2 million and EUR2.14 billion. Keep the companion disagreement; the tabletop does not investigate upstream statistical definitions.
Paragraph 32 records monthly party meetings under the Embassy of Slovakia and refers to good offices. Preserve the external convenor and unknown participant count.
Paragraph 11 counts 18 political parties. This is neither 18 meetings nor 18 people.
Paragraph 18 describes over a hundred information-exchange instances. Preserve the strict lower bound and reporting period; do not add unlike custody counts.
Paragraph 5 supports 14,000 ground and air patrols. Buffer-zone patrol work is not displaced by a source register or political referral.
Paragraphs 38-39 support good-offices assessments and the existing dual-hatted representative. No new approval or organizational merger follows.
Paragraph 27 counts 297 organized/supported activities, of which 46 were intercommunal, as of 31 May. The subset is not an additional 46 activities.
Paragraph 14 records 95 Deputy Special Adviser meetings and unheld regional consultations due to budget/liquidity pressures. Neither gives an avoidable-cost amount.
Paragraph 1 and Annex I heading identify a Greek Cypriot leader submission. The selected obligation concerns authorship only; the annex's substantive claims are not adjudicated.
Annex II heading identifies the Turkish Cypriot side. Inclusion within a UN report is not Secretariat endorsement; no party assertions are promoted.
Paragraph 17 records approval of 30 sites on 5 May and work begun. Completion of those sites is not claimed at this stage.
Paragraph 20 supports approximately 74% of EUR1 million utilized by 11 June 2025 under phase two. Utilization is not an efficiency or savings measure.

Paragraph 44 records finalized enlargement discussions in the June-December 2024 period and refers to the unrevised symbol. Do not infer actual construction or substitute a revised historical release.
The cover gives S/2025/7/Rev.1, 14 January 2025; paragraphs 1-2 give the earlier reporting interval. January 3 is a requested deadline, not verified publication of the absent original.
Paragraph 30 supports first-week-of-December commencement at the existing crossing. Preserve limited date precision and the companion referral.
Paragraph 19 gives UNDP implementation, early-December start and envisaged end-January completion. The completion date remains prospective in this source.
Paragraph 9 says no concrete results on opening new crossings. This is source-period status, not a statement that existing-crossing enlargement never occurred.
Paragraph 20 and footnote 1 support UNFICYP facilitation, committee auspices and S/2026/9 referral. The adjacent figure is outside this selected count-free obligation.

Paragraph 18 describes two different actions: information exchanged in 202 instances, and three individuals in custody exchanged. The inherited prose attaches both to information exchange; its structured custody field partially preserves the distinction. Request a semantic correction.
Paragraph 15 gives 151 meetings across 13 committees under good-offices auspices with UNFICYP support. Those are existing support roles, not a new consolidation.
Paragraph 17 says all agreed cemeteries were renovated. Scope remains the agreed initiative; no numeric total from the later expanded portfolio is imported.
Paragraph 22 gives approximately 86% as of November without restating allocation. Do not backfill an unchanged EUR1 million denominator from an earlier report.
Paragraph 32 gives March, Humanitarian Matters as lead, Youth support and companion referral. No exact day or headcount is supplied.
Paragraph 25 gives the workshop title and Humanitarian Affairs/Youth roles, but no exact date or count. Preserve the distinct labels instead of silently standardizing the source.
Paragraph 12 refers readers to UNFICYP for detail on the fragile buffer zone. Referral is not independent factual corroboration or operational substitution.
Paragraph 4 retains the UNFICYP operational account. The selected obligation is boundary preservation, not verification of every incident in the report.
Paragraph 19 says an event marked completion in February and describes UNDP implementation. The ceremony month is not a verified exact physical-completion date.
Paragraph 32 retains additional crossings as unimplemented initiatives. Keep this separate from the completed enlargement of an existing crossing.
Paragraph 20 concerns approximately 70 sites with completed, ongoing or preparatory activities. No completed-site subtotal is available.
Paragraph 18 gives 174 meetings across 13 committees with support roles. Do not combine with the 128 different stakeholder meetings without record-level linkage.
Paragraph 17 counts 128 stakeholder meetings. Its denominator is distinct from committee meetings and is retained separately.

Paragraph 29 says over EUR1.7 million since inception in 2019, alongside approximately 67% of EUR1.5 million for 2023-2026. The inherited lower-bound field prevents an exact-total claim, but the prose omits over and the field lacks an explicit strict comparator. Request qualification hardening, not a claim that the number is wrong.

amendments.source_excerpt: exchanged information on 202 instances and exchanged three individuals in custody
amendments.proposed_assertion: Through the Joint Contact Rooms, the Technical Committee on Crime and Criminal Matters exchanged information in 202 instances and separately exchanged three individuals in custody. These are different actions and units.
amendments.reason: The original summary collapses distinct action predicates even though its structured fields distinguish the counts.

amendments.source_excerpt: Over 1.7 million euros have been utilized
amendments.proposed_assertion: Phase two was extended through 2026. By June 2026 approximately 67% of EUR1.5 million allocated for 2023-2026 had been utilized; more than EUR1.7 million had been utilized since inception in 2019. The two amounts have different perimeters and are not savings.
amendments.reason: The lower-bound field is retained, but strictness and inception period should survive rendering as explicit qualifications.

scenario_answers.SC01: Retain one visit identity with source-specific starts of 27 and 28 January. No majority correction or additional visit count.
scenario_answers.SC02: Keep more than 30 participants and adoption of the workplan. Do not claim exactly 30 or implemented outcomes.
scenario_answers.SC03: CNMC remains a separate function; 17 December 2024 remains pre-window context; the publication is not another workshop.
scenario_answers.SC04: Attribute the announcement to the 3 April UNOWAS briefing and its 9 June UNOCA reference. Actual withdrawal is not inferred.
scenario_answers.SC05: Retain both export comparators and source definitions. Do not compute one cross-report trade/export ratio.
scenario_answers.SC06: Keep planned September start, actual early-December commencement and February completion-marking event as different stages. Additional crossings are a separate unimplemented scope.
scenario_answers.SC07: Retain Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot authorship without Secretariat endorsement. Use the 14 January revision, not an invented January 3 original.
scenario_answers.SC08: Keep the initial agreed cemetery initiative separate from the approximately 70-site mixed-stage portfolio. No completed-site total is derived.
scenario_answers.SC09: Do not compare 74%, 86% and 67% as an efficiency trend. Preserve phase, period and allocation; proposed amendment AM11-02 explicitly restores over EUR1.7m since 2019.
scenario_answers.SC10: Separate activities, subsets, meetings, members, parties, information-exchange instances and people. AM11-01 corrects the action attached to the custody count; no cross-unit total.
scenario_answers.SC11: Four different synthetic actors at 20 minutes each contribute 80 person-minutes. Common work counts once in actual burden. Missing time remains unknown and blocks a complete-process contrast.
scenario_answers.SC12: A synthetic faster shadow containing a material misattribution must be quarantined and cannot advance. Preserve its effort and failure; no live incident or workload gain is asserted.

source_access_note: Original retained PDF/HTML bytes were used. Browser retrieval and screenshot attempts for selected originals were unavailable; no source substitutes or new cohort records were added.
